<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 688a39d7700f3b3195e3bd782f42f25622cb4327` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4051c1349a39050b6a947990f3dcd7138ac28654`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed read-only against the brief's inputs: card #23308 (body, claim 6151102268, dispatch 6151126677, report 6154629520), the 7a blocker 6150594560 and measurement 6151042307 on #22975, PR #23258's body (`09ef77c7d8`), PR #23334 (body, file list, the three-dot diff against `origin/main` `cc14657ede`, the merge ref `8260e4f245`), `permission-set-projection.ts` at S8's parent `99e944daf2`, ADR-0131 D3/D4/D6 on `origin/main`, the WHICH LEVEL rule in `pr-automation.yml`, and the head's check-runs. Where a judgment needed a reader this PR feeds, I read it on `origin/main`: `security-catalog.ts` (core), `resolve-authz-context.ts`, `protocol.ts` (write-through, projector dispatch, delete heal, `isArtifactBacked`), `metadata-manager.ts` (`registerInMemory`, `unregister`), `registry.ts` (`getItem`), `app-plugin.ts` (the in-memory security collections) and the metadata-type table. The eight files in the PR's file list equal the three-dot diff and the merge ref's diff against `main`; the merge ref also carries five `main` commits the head predates (see ③).

### ① Derived judgments

**Parity with S8's parent on an environment kernel.**
- The echoed body is the same shape. The parent's `syncEvaluatorRegistry` registered, under `permission`, the overlay body through `stripDecorations` (the same six decorations plus the marker; the function moved byte-for-byte), `_provenance: 'org'` only when `tenantAuthored`, `_packageId` only when `tenantAuthored` and the binding read answered, and `_envProjection: true`. `echoSecurityCatalogMutation` builds the identical object. `tenantAuthored` for a permission set is the same call, `classifyPackagedPermissionSet(name, ql, { status: 'read', envelope }).status === 'org'`, over the same layered envelope; the owner is the same `readServedPackageBinding` (now typed) with the same warn-and-register-unowned fallback. On a `packaged` or `unknown` verdict the parent echoed an unstamped body; the new module skips the name when the registry serves it and otherwise registers it unstamped, the same as before. I found no permission set the new echo stamps `org` that the parent would not have.
- Which names are echoed: the parent echoed every overlay-backed name; the new module additionally requires that the engine registry not serve the name. On an environment kernel the registry holds no stored row (`applyRegistryWriteThrough` returns at `environmentId !== undefined`, and `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` declines there), so for a metadata-door set the two conditions select the same names. The extra condition only removes echoes the catalog never read (registry first).
- Two places the new echo serves a set the parent would not have, both in failure modes and both a stored, active overlay: (a) the parent gated the echo on the `sys_permission_set` upsert reporting `seeded + updated + unchanged` above zero, so a refused row write left the set unechoed; the new module has no row write and no such gate; (b) the parent's reconcile read `sys_metadata` through `tryFind(..., 1000)`, so overlays past the thousandth row were never re-echoed after a restart; the boot pass reads without a limit (the engine's `fillQueryAstDefaults` adds none, and nothing in `driver-sql` caps it), so every active env-wide overlay is echoed. Neither serves a set the parent refused by policy; the overlay is the authoritative definition (ADR-0094 D1, ADR-0131 D3).
- Positions: a new capability, judged below.

**The dev's deviation.**
- The registry check: `registry.getItem(type, name)` answers the bare slot first, then any package-prefixed composite entry, so it is true for every stored row a host kernel hydrated and for every artifact a package registered in the engine registry. For `permission` that is the complete set of declared artifacts (manifest `permissions` are registry items). For `position` it is not: stack-declared positions are not registry items at all. The catalog's own measurement (header table in `security-catalog.ts`) counts 0 positions in the engine registry and 10 in the metadata service, and `app-plugin.ts` registers them there through `registerInMemory('position', ...)` in its `SECURITY_FIELDS` loop. So "a name the engine registry already serves" is the right test for a host kernel's stored rows and for declared permission sets, and an incomplete test for declared positions. Consequence next.
- Shadowing a declared artifact: `permission` and `position` are both `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false` (metadata-plugin.zod.ts 1177-1178); D6's whole-item replacement is the five presentational types only, so no legitimate D6 overlay of either type exists. For a permission set the lock gate on the metadata door refuses an overlay of an artifact-backed name, and a legacy pre-rollback overlay was echoed unstamped on the parent but never read by the catalog (registry first): on both trees the catalog served the declared body, so nothing goes unserved and nothing is newly served as declared. For a position the door's seal, `isSealedManagedItem`, asks `isArtifactBacked`, which reads the registry's artifact items only, and no `position` authoring gate is registered (gates exist for `object` and `permission`). Nothing I read in the door refuses a metadata-door `position` save under a stack-declared position's name. If such a row exists on an environment kernel, the new echo registers it in the metadata service over the app's in-memory declaration (last write wins), the catalog then serves the row's `permissionSets` instead of the declaration, and the boot pass repeats that on every restart. The parent never echoed positions, so on an environment kernel the declaration kept winning. A host kernel already serves the row on both trees (the write-through hydrates the bare slot; registry first). This is the one place I can name where the change serves something on an environment kernel that S8's parent would have served as the declared item: a metadata author's overlay of a stack-declared position's binding list. The actor is a `manage_metadata` holder under `single` or the operator under a wall (ADR-0131 D3). Escalated as ③-1 with a guard that fits inside the new module.
- A deleted set, or an uninstalled package's set: `deleteMetaItem` runs `restoreArtifactRegistryView` (which re-registers only on a control-plane kernel) and then awaits the projector with state `deleted`; the layered read has no overlay, `current` is our echo, `dropEcho` unregisters it. `deletePackage` deletes each row the same way (protocol 26948-26975), so no own uninstall code is needed. Boot-test leg 7 measured both on the environment kernel (resolve undefined, read refused). On a host kernel the echo never exists to leak: the write-through hydrates before the projector runs (22274 before 22299), and the boot restore (`restoreMetadataFromDb`, called from `ObjectQLPlugin` start, as the namespace module's cold-boot account states) precedes `kernel:ready`, so the boot pass skips every stored row there; the leak removal in `dropEcho` is a belt for the registry heal the dogfood run caught. A disabled (not uninstalled) runtime package: the catalog hides an item whose `_packageId` the registry reports disabled; the echo carries the binding; parity. A second replica of an environment kernel: the cluster replay (protocol 7607-7623) re-runs the write-through and the heal but no projector, so a save or delete on one replica changes nothing in another's metadata service until that replica restarts. That is the parent's behaviour too (projector-based); a deleted set stays served on the other replica until restart on both trees. NOT MEASURED.
- Removing heal-to-declared: safe for `permission`, because every declared set is a registry item, is never echoed, and keeps being served registry-first after the overlay goes. Not safe for a stack-declared position: once the echo has overwritten the app's in-memory declaration, the overlay's delete makes `dropEcho` remove the only entry, and the position confers nothing until restart. That is a narrowing (fail-closed), and it is the other half of ③-1.

**Positions.**
- The echo for `position` has the same shape as for `permission`, under the `position` type. The catalog's `fromMetadata` applies `servable` only: an object whose `name` matches, owner from `_packageId`, disabled-package rule. No type-specific shape test, so the reader accepts it; boot-test leg 5 proves the resolver reads it end to end (the holder is granted through the set the position names), and leg 7 that it survives a sibling's delete.
- A position echo whose `permissionSets` names a set the catalog cannot resolve: `positionBoundSetNames` reads the names from the definition; `catalogSetBody` returns undefined for a name `resolve('permission', name)` does not answer, which "confers nothing"; the activation ledger filter (`readDisabledCatalogNames`) is applied independently. Fail-closed, no throw.
- `_provenance: 'org'` is unconditional for a position. For a position row a code package materialized through the door (allowRuntimeCreate), that is the stamp a host kernel's hydrator applies to every stored row (`stateTenantAuthorship`), so it is parity with the host and display only.
- Built-ins (`everyone`, `guest`) are registry items (`declareEveryoneBaseline`), registered at the earlier `kernel:ready` hook (security-plugin.ts 1741) ahead of the boot pass (4536), and never echoed; a metadata-door save under their names is skipped by the registry check.

**The boot pass.**
- Selection: `sys_metadata` rows with `type` in `permission`, `permissions`, `position`, `positions` and `state: 'active'`, read under `seedCtx()` (system, no tenant), then every row with a non-null `organization_id` skipped; the name set per type is run through the same mutation echo, so a name whose layered read has no overlay, or that the registry serves, is skipped again. Active, env-wide, the two types: correct.
- Order: `runBootstrap` is the last `kernel:ready` hook SecurityPlugin registers, and `dispatchHookPropagating` runs handlers in registration order. The pass runs before `reconcileAudienceBindingSuggestions` at the end of the same function (4523). On the live path the awaited projector precedes `emitMetadataMutation` in save (22274, 22299, 22306), publish (23691, 23775, 23783) and delete (28185, 28210, 28216), so the #22801 listener's reconcile reads an echoed catalog. One caveat, identical on the parent: `declareEveryone` is a separate, earlier `kernel:ready` hook (1741 on the head, 1751 on the parent), so after a restart `everyone` is derived before the pass; an accepted runtime-package set is picked up at the next permission mutation. Fail-closed. The first request: the boot test's `kernel.bootstrap()` resolves after `kernel:ready`; whether a given host serves before `kernel:ready` settles is the server composition's property, unchanged by this PR and shared with the parent's reconcile.
- Unreadable table: a throwing `find` is logged at `warn` with the consequence and the pass continues with the other type; boot continues and the catalog is partial for that type, each missing name fail-closed. The parent's `tryFind` swallowed the same failure as `[]` with no line at all, so this is louder. It is not a boot failure and not `error`; under AGENTS.md's one question (does the system look normal while something it claims persisted has not landed?) the answer is no, nothing is claimed persisted and the affected users are refused visibly, so `warn` is the level the rule assigns. The unit case pins the warn.

**Prohibitions from the dispatch.**
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is not in the file list.
- No `sys_permission_set` write: the new module's only engine access is the `sys_metadata` read; the plugin diff adds no write; the edit-surface case pins `engine.tables.sys_permission_set` empty.
- `permission-set-projection.ts` is present and unwired (no `registerPermissionSetProjection` or `reconcilePermissionSetProjection` call remains in `security-plugin.ts`); it imports `isProjectionEcho`, `readServedPackageBinding` and `stripDecorations` from the new module and nothing imports it but `index.ts` (unchanged exports), so 7a's deletion is a pure removal. No import cycle: the lock imports only `@objectstack/metadata-core`; `organization-scope.ts` imports nothing.
- A1 was not built.

**The pins.**
- The boot test wires nothing itself: it imports `SecurityPlugin` and `appSecurityPluginOptions` only, never the echo module; the environment legs assert anti-vacuity (`registry.getItem` falsy, `source: 'metadata'`), the refused-then-granted read, one pending `everyone` suggestion, the unowned no-package set, the position, a restart with the stored rows confirmed through an own `better-sqlite3` connection, and the two retirements. The host control has no restart leg.
- Ablations: reported by the dev (hook unregistered: 7 environment legs red, host green; boot pass removed: the restart leg and the leg after it red). No ablation case is committed, so the record weighs them as the dev's evidence. The restart leg's dependence on the boot pass follows from the code: the metadata service starts empty and nothing else registers these two types on an environment kernel.
- #23258's six cases all run on the new module. Case 3 (edit surface) now pins no `sys_permission_set` row instead of the row's `managed_by: 'admin'`, which is the post-S8 truth, and keeps the lock, editable and deletable assertions; case 6 asserts the outcome `registered` instead of `seeded: 1` and keeps the unowned echo and the single warn. The anti-vacuity assertions are retained. Not weakened.
- The #21789 pair: the `org` stamp case is re-homed verbatim. The control changed from "a legacy overlay of a code-shipped set is echoed unstamped" to "a name the registry already serves is not echoed", which is a behaviour change the PR body discloses, and a narrowing of what the layered read's `code` layer shows; the catalog read the registry first on both trees.
- New cases cover drop, skip, leak removal, drafts and foreign types, the boot pass's selection (plural spelling, org rows skipped) and its unreadable-table warn. The declared-position control registers its position in the engine registry, which is not the shape a stack declares (metadata service); see ③-1.

**Published text.**
- Changeset: accurate; "they change nothing a host kernel resolves" holds because host hydration precedes both the projector and the pass. "In the security catalog again" is true of permission sets; the next paragraph states positions never were, so the text is not misleading.
- Module JSDoc: "A position is always tenant-authored at that point, because only names no artifact declares are echoed" is false for a stack-declared position, which lives only in the metadata service and is not seen by the registry check (③-1). Everything else in the header matches the code.
- `permission-set-projection.ts`: the replacement comments are accurate; the module's own header still describes the retired row projection, which 7a deletes.
- `security-plugin.ts` 4349-4355 names the echo as the environment-kernel path: accurate.
- Docs: `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 11 (the write-through is no longer registered) stays true; no hand-written page states the environment-kernel behaviour either way; ADR-0094, 0126 and 0131 anchor the projection file, which is kept.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, agreed. `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts` is not in the file list; the new module's exports are not re-exported from the entry; `readServedPackageBinding` gains an optional third parameter but was module-private before and stays off the entry. No new accepted key or value: the `position` type and `PositionSchema.permissionSets` exist already, and the change is which kernel serves a stored row. Under WHICH LEVEL a `fix(` that changes no public surface stays `patch`; the position capability is behaviour on one topology, not a published surface, so the dispatch's "unless your measurement finds a surface S8's parent did not have" is not triggered. With `no` declared, `check-changeset-no-major`'s level axis stands down, so the level is this record's to judge, and it stands.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Escalated to the seat, act before the queue.** A metadata-door `position` row whose name a stack declares is now echoed over the app's in-memory declaration on an environment kernel, and the boot pass repeats it each restart; the overlay's delete then removes the declaration until restart. The door does not refuse such a row (`isArtifactBacked` reads the registry's artifacts; no `position` gate), and a host kernel already serves it, so the new behaviour is host parity, not a new door, and the actor is a metadata author. It is still the one way this change serves, on an environment kernel, a definition S8's parent would have served as declared, and the module's own JSDoc premise is false for it. Recommended, inside the dispatch's file surface: in `echoSecurityCatalogMutation`, treat a metadata-service item of the name that is not our echo as declared and skip (the mirror of `registryServes`), with a pin whose declared position is registered through the metadata service rather than the engine registry. If the seat prefers, the same goes to a card against the door (protocol.ts, seat 1's region) and this PR lands as is; either way the dev's JSDoc line should be corrected.
2. `dropEcho` on the registry-serves branch calls `metadata.unregister` while the overlay row still exists; the inline comment "the stored row is already gone" is true only on the delete branch. `MetadataManager.unregister` deletes through loaders whose protocol is `datasource:` with write capability. In both compositions reviewed none is registered: `NodeMetadataManager` carries a `FilesystemLoader` and the plugin's `MemoryLoader` (`memory:`), and `setDatabaseDriver` fires only when the manager is constructed with both `datasource` and `driver`, and skips itself on an environment kernel. Latent, not live, and it also announces a spurious `deleted` watcher and realtime event for a name that is still served. Recommend an in-memory-only drop on that branch or a corrected comment. Not blocking.
3. Deviations, each answered: (a) registry-served names are not echoed, accepted for `permission`, incomplete for `position` (item 1); (b) heal-to-declared removed, accepted for `permission`, the narrowing half of item 1 for positions; (c) the #21789 control replaced, disclosed, a narrowing of the layered read's display only.
4. The dev lists no open questions. Mine is item 1's control shape.
5. NOT MEASURED: a real cloud kernel (the factory file is outside this repository, as the dev's measurement states); a host-kernel restart with the hook wired (no host restart leg; by ordering the boot pass is a no-op there); a multi-replica environment kernel (the echo is per-process and the cluster replay runs no projector, parity with the parent); the ablations (dev-reported); dogfood and the `@objectstack/cli` integration tier as the dev's local runs, since PR CI skipped the dogfood shards (#22998) and whether Test Core executes the cli `integration` project was not verified here; the five `main` commits between the dev's last merge (`87e902dcbb`) and `origin/main` (`cc14657ede`), which are in the merge ref but not in the dev's local gate runs; one of them (`37510aa0f9`, ADR-0138 guest grants) edits `security-plugin.ts` in other regions, merges cleanly, and folds no positions for a guest, so it does not read the echo.
6. Check-runs on the head, polled at 2026-10-13T20:47Z: 32 completed success, 6 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, the packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 1 still running: Test Core (3/6). Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not pre-judge the running shard.
7. Out of scope, found: the metadata door's D6 seal cannot see a metadata-service-declared position (pre-existing on host kernels; protocol.ts). The `everyone` derivation at the earlier `kernel:ready` hook runs before the boot pass on both trees (fail-closed until the next permission mutation).

Adopted by `domain:engine` seat 2 at 2026-10-13T20:50Z, after a tool-use audit of the isolated reviewer's transcript. The reviewer made reads, `git fetch` into review refs, REST GETs, and record writes only. It made no GitHub write and ran no build, test or gate. The seat takes the verdict as PASS, and the PR is held for one small patch round before the queue:
- **③-1 is fixed in this PR**, with the reviewer's recommended remedy. `echoSecurityCatalogMutation` skips a name the kernel's metadata service already holds as a non-echo item: a stack-declared position, for instance, which the registry check cannot see. A pin registers a declared position through the metadata service and shows that an overlay neither shadows it nor deletes it. On this authorization path, deleting an overlay must never take away a declared item until restart.
- **③-2 is fixed in the same round:** the drop is in-memory only, so no `datasource:` delete and no spurious `deleted` event.
- **The JSDoc premise** ("a position is always tenant-authored") is corrected.
